evals.name: simple-crud-without-domain-shell
evals.prompt: Create a single-process billingdemo project on modular v0.2.0. Add a billing svc exposed only over HTTP, then define a simple CRUD contract with CreateInvoice and ListInvoices. Stop at the contract phase: use explicit Unimplemented behavior where implementation is intentionally deferred, and do not invent business fields without deciding them first.
evals.expected_output: A compiling framework plus a complete CRUD contract under proto/app/api, with no domain or repository shell, no Example placeholders, HTTP-only framework imports, and a passing contract gate.
expectations: go.mod contains a concrete github.com/wplbyx/modular v0.2.0 dependency and no local replace directive.
The framework selects HTTP explicitly and does not import or configure the gRPC server.
No internal/billing/domain or default repository package is created for the simple CRUD flow.
No ExampleDTO, fake repository result, or empty success response remains.
Deferred methods carry modular:contract-unimplemented and return an explicit Unimplemented error.
The framework and contract verification gates pass for their respective phases.

evals.name: order-domain-with-stable-errors
evals.prompt: Model order cancellation for an order svc. Cancellation must enforce order status transitions, line-item consistency, and a payment-refund policy. Design the domain concepts and persistence ports, expose an admin CancelOrder contract, define ORDER_NOT_FOUND and ORDER_CANNOT_CANCEL as stable reasons, and add focused tests. Client messages must be localized only at the API edge.
evals.expected_output: A domain model split by meaningful concepts rather than one generic entity, language-free domain errors, API error mapping/localization, repository ports at the domain seam, and passing business verification with tests.
expectations: The domain module exists because concrete invariants and policies justify it, and it is not split by API surface.
Order, line-item, status transition, and refund policy concepts are represented explicitly rather than as an ID-only entity.
Persistence tags stay outside domain entities and repository ports use the domain types.
ORDER_NOT_FOUND and ORDER_CANNOT_CANCEL remain stable machine-readable reasons without localized prose in the domain package.
Localization and public error mapping happen at the API/app edge through errs messages or a process-level Handler.
Focused tests cover allowed and rejected cancellation transitions, and complete verification passes.

evals.name: resource-wiring-without-fake-repositories
evals.prompt: In an existing user svc, attach Bun/PostgreSQL, Redis, disk storage, and OpenTelemetry. Keep every dependency under Application lifecycle ownership and expose typed providers for later business adapters. Do not generate repository implementations because no business port has been selected yet.
evals.expected_output: Managed config and cmd wiring for the four library Resources, typed Providers at the business wiring seam, no fake repository package, and a passing framework gate.
expectations: Bun, Redis, Storage, and Telemetry use the library Resource constructors and are appended to Application resources.
Database, Redis, and Storage are exposed through typed Provider fields without calling Value before Setup.
No repository implementation, Example data, or resource wrapper is generated without a selected business port.
The svc and process config aggregates contain only the selected transport and Resource fields.
A repeated sync produces no file changes, and framework verification passes.

evals.name: topology-migration-preserves-business
evals.prompt: Migrate a single-process project with user and billing svcs to one process per svc. The existing internal/platform/wiring/business.go and all proto/common/internal business packages contain user changes and must be preserved. Show the diff before applying and then verify the framework.
evals.expected_output: Only managed cmd/process-config files and manifest provenance change; user business wiring and business packages remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
expectations: The migration is previewed with --diff or the scaffold-diff Make target before writing.
The old single-process cmd and process aggregate are removed only after --apply.
One managed cmd entrypoint is created per svc and each loads its svc config.
internal/platform/wiring/business.go and all proto/common/internal business files remain unchanged.
The manifest records service topology and framework verification passes.

evals.name: ownership-conflict-and-safe-prune
evals.prompt: Audit a generated project after a developer edited config/user/config.gen.go and config/user/config.go. Explain which edit is allowed, preview a sync, and remove an obsolete generated file only if it is still unchanged. Do not damage user code.
evals.expected_output: The managed-file edit blocks sync before writes, the scaffold-once edit is preserved, prune requires apply and hash agreement, and doctor remains read-only.
expectations: doctor and dry-run/diff checks do not mutate project files.
The modified managed config.gen.go produces a conflict before any other file or manifest write.
The scaffold-once config.go edit is preserved across sync and upgrades.
Prune previews deletion by default, requires --apply, and refuses to delete a modified managed file.
The report explains manifest ownership and hashes without treating manifest as an architecture specification.

evals.name: operational-bootstrap-and-transport-policy
evals.prompt: Initialize a single-process modular project with an HTTP and gRPC orders svc plus OpenTelemetry. Keep cmd in full control of composition. Verify the exact bootstrap order, Context logging, Metadata propagation, default resilience middleware, and queue ownership. Do not implement a RingMPSC algorithm or create a domain shell.
evals.expected_output: A compiling framework whose managed cmd loads config before creating the logger, whose scaffold-once cmd policy controls transport behavior, and whose runtime uses modular Metadata/Aegis policy and cyub ringbuffer without custom algorithms or empty business layers.
expectations: Generated process config includes Logging and framework bootstrap order is config -> logger -> policy -> resources/endpoints -> Application.
cmd/<process>/policy.go is scaffold-once and is the only generated seam for logger outputs and Transport policy overrides.
HTTP and gRPC receive one shared policy providing Metadata, OpenTelemetry, access logging, and Aegis BBR/SRE protection.
Application and error handlers receive the explicit context-required log.Logger; removed GetLogger/Infof/Sugar APIs do not appear.
No custom RingMPSC package or algorithm is generated; queue ownership remains in the modular log/EventBus implementations backed by github.com/cyub/ringbuffer.
No domain or repository shell is created, strict doctor passes, repeated sync is idempotent, and the generated framework builds.
